reason: Example: K-quasiconformal equivalence of A(1,2) and A(1,R) forces log R <= K log 2 (annular distortion clause applied to the inverse), so A(1,2) and A(1,8) are not 2-quasiconformally equivalent; the parameter is distorted by a factor in [1/K,K] both ways; no round annulus is K-quasiconformally equivalent to D* because the distortion applied to h^{-1} would give 2 pi/log(R/r) = mu(Gamma_{r,R}) <= K mu(Gamma_{D*}) = 0.
